title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: which excess withdrawal fees of a reconciled cycle cover a withdrawal
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to a Savings & Money Market Accounts account from which overdraft protection transfers have been made, when the excess withdrawal fees of a statement cycle are reconciled. It fixes how many of the counted withdrawals beyond the allowance a fee already covers.

## Policy clause

1. An excess withdrawal fee entry of the cycle covers a counted withdrawal beyond the allowance unless it has been refunded as a bank error, because a fee assessed contrary to the charter covers no withdrawal.
2. A fee refunded as a courtesy was correctly assessed and still covers its withdrawal.
3. Every excess withdrawal fee of the cycle assessed contrary to the charter has been refunded before the fees owed are counted. Where that condition does not yet hold, the fees owed for the cycle are not counted.

The number of withdrawals that fees cover is the number of excess withdrawal fee entries of the cycle less the number of those refunded as a bank error.

## Basis of decision

- **Authority.** Fee entries and refund entries, with their fee type, refund ground and statement cycle, are read from the savings account's transaction record.
- **Object correlation.** Only excess withdrawal fees of the reconciled cycle and their refunds enter the figure.

## Input, judgement, output

| Entry of the reconciled cycle | Covers a withdrawal? |
|---|---|
| excess withdrawal fee entry, not refunded | yes |
| excess withdrawal fee entry refunded as a bank error | no |
| excess withdrawal fee entry refunded as a courtesy | yes; it was correctly assessed |
| monthly maintenance fee entry | no; not an excess withdrawal fee |

## Worked case (hypothetical cycle)

The cycle carries three excess withdrawal fee entries. One was attached to a withdrawal that never counted toward the allowance and has been refunded as a bank error. Another received a courtesy refund. The fees cover three less one, which is two withdrawals: the courtesy refund does not stop a fee covering its withdrawal, the bank-error refund does.

## Points of judgement

**Wrong reading:** "Every fee entry in the cycle covers a withdrawal." **Correct basis:** a fee refunded as a bank error covers no withdrawal.

**Wrong reading:** "A courtesy refund also stops the fee covering its withdrawal." **Correct basis:** only a bank-error refund does.
